numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Calling np.resize with an unsigned NumPy integer as the new size (np.uint32(1)) emits a RuntimeWarning 'overflow encountered in scalar negative' from the line repeats = -(-new_size // a.size), then raises SystemError: <built-in function concatenate> returned NULL without setting an exception. With np.uint64(1) it raises OverflowError: cannot fit 'numpy.uint64' into an index-sized integer. The negation of the unsigned value underflows and yields a large positive repeats, which causes allocation failures and/or swapping.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: np.resize should return the same result as with the signed input np.int32(1), i.e. the array [23] for np.resize(np.array([[23, 95], [66, 37]]), new_size=1), with no warning and no exception.
trigger_conditions: second argument new_size is an unsigned integer NumPy scalar such as np.uint32 or np.uint64
affected in NumPy 2.x (tested on v2.3.0 and v2.2.5), may affect other versions
the input array a is non-empty, so the code reaches the ceil-division repeats computation

input_output_examples.buggy_output: RuntimeWarning: overflow encountered in scalar negative; SystemError: <built-in function concatenate> returned

numerical_characteristics.dtype: np.uint32 and np.uint64 (unsigned new_shape argument to np.resize); reference int32/int64 succeed
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: new_size of 1 passed as unsigned integer; negation of unsigned value underflows to a large positive repeats value
category_specific_evidence: Original code computed repeats = -(-new_size // a.size); negating an unsigned new_size underflows and produces a large positive repeats, per PR body.
Issue reports RuntimeWarning: overflow encountered in scalar negative for np.uint32(1) input, followed by SystemError from concatenate.
For np.uint64(1), issue reports OverflowError: cannot fit 'numpy.uint64' into an index-sized integer.
Fix replaces negation with repeats = (new_size + a.size - 1) // a.size (ceiling division without negating new_size).
Added test_unsigned_resize asserts np.resize(arr, np.int32(1)) equals np.resize(arr, np.uint32(1)) and np.resize(arr, np.int64(1)) equals np.resize(arr, np.uint64(1)) for arr = [[23, 95], [66, 37]].
Issue affects NumPy 2.x (tested v2.3.0 and v2.2.5).
reproduction_risks: Reproduction must use an unsigned scalar new_shape (np.uint32/np.uint64) to trigger the underflow; signed int32/int64 do not exhibit it.
Exact failure mode depends on platform and version: uint32 gave SystemError, uint64 gave OverflowError in the reported environment.
Expected-value comparison relies on the signed-int result as reference; no independent numeric tolerance is stated.
